explanation: During droughts, elephants sometimes gouge the soft, spongy wood to get at the stored water. The trunk can visibly shrink in the dry season and swell after rain.

claims.text: Baobab trees store large amounts of water in their thick, soft trunks.
Acacias, mahogany trees and ebony trees do not store water in swollen trunks.
Elephants sometimes strip and gouge baobab wood to get moisture, especially in droughts.
Baobab trunks shrink in the dry season and expand after rain as their water content changes.
